text:
alin: Quick sync request — we need a single agreed error taxonomy for the new reliability dashboards. Runtime, infra, and console teams keep sending slightly different metrics and the dashboards are diverging. Can we decide on canonical metric names/labels today?

maria: +1. Main things we need: total timeouts, user-facing 5xx, OOMs, and degraded-mode/fallback counts. Also quota rejects should be separate (quota vs healthy fallback).

kevin: Proposed minimal metric set from runtime side:
```
redwood.errors.count{reason="timeout|5xx|oom|fallback|quota_reject"}
redwood.errors.latency_histogram
redwood.inference.fallbacks.count{fallback_type="model_variant|region|graceful_degrade"}
```
We can emit reason and fallback_type as tags. But worried about label cardinality if we include full model names and route ids.

zane: Agree on low-cardinality labels. Suggest labels: env, model_family, route_owner, reason. For model use model_family (e.g., gpt-3-like, redwood-1) not full variant id. For routes, use route_owner or route_group instead of raw route name.

maria: For 5xx we need to be explicit: only count user-facing 5xx (i.e., responses returned to clients with 5xx). Internal infra retries that never surface should be separate metric: redwood.internal.failures.count. Otherwise the SLO math gets messy.

kevin: Good call. Runtime can emit both: redwood.request.errors.user.count and redwood.request.errors.internal.count. User-facing labels: status_class=5xx|4xx|timeout etc.

alin: What about timeouts — we have two flavors: frontend request-level timeouts (API gateway) and model-side token-generation timeouts. We should capture both.

zane: Suggest two metrics: redwood.request.timeout.frontend.count and redwood.request.timeout.model.count. Keep them separate in dashboards, but show a combined "total timeouts" rollup.

opsbot: Deploy alert: grafana/dashboard-updater deployed to prod (commit 3f9b).

maria: OOMs: runtime can detect device OOMs and OOM during compilation. We should capture OOM severity (hard OOM vs recovered oom via fallback). Proposed labels: oom_severity=fatal|recovered, affected_component=executor|loader. Metric: redwood.runtime.oom.count{oom_severity, affected_component, model_family}.

kevin: Implementation note: we must avoid tagging with request_id or prompt_hash. Use prompt_hash_sampled if we need example tracing but not as a metric label.

alin: Quotas: quota rejects should be separate with reason tags: quota_type=rate|concurrency|billing. redwood.quota.rejections.count{quota_type, plan_tier}. We should display per-plan-tier trends in the console for revenue/ops correlation.

zane: Dashboard layout draft: 1) Top row: SLOs and overall success rate (1 - user_errors_per_min). 2) Row: error breakdown stacked (timeouts / 5xx / OOM / fallback / quota). 3) Heatmap: model_family vs route_owner showing error rates. 4) Timeseries: fallback counts and fallout by fallback_type. 5) Alerts and note of sampling.

maria: Alert thresholds: start conservative. Example: error_rate_5m > 1% AND error_count > 50 -> paging. We should also have degraded_mode_rate alert if fallback ratio > 5% for 15m.

kevin: PromQL snippets for dashboard panels (draft):
```
# user 5xx rate
sum by (model_family) (rate(redwood.request.errors.user.count{status_class="5xx"}[5m]))

# fallback ratio per model_family
sum by (model_family) (rate(redwood.inference.fallbacks.count[5m]))
/
sum by (model_family) (rate(redwood.requests.count[5m]))
```

alin: Telemetry pipeline: runtime emits raw metrics to prometheus pushgateway -> infra aggregates and forwards to long-term metrics. We need clear ownership of which metric is authoritative. Decision: runtime emits canonical, infra applies aggregation and stores backups. Console/dashboard reads from infra store.

zane: Can infra add derived metric names (e.g., redwood.errors.total.rollup) but always keep the raw runtime metric name in place so we can trace back?

maria: Yes, but document mapping. Also note that derived metrics must be recomputable from raw metrics — avoid opaque counters done only in infra.

kevin: UX ask: console rollout page wants a per-deployment "reliability signal" (error budget burn, fallback ratio) shown for canary windows. We'll need a short-timescale rollup (1m). Can the runtime emit 1m buckets?

zane: Runtime will emit counters; infra will provide rate() at different windows. 1m is fine but watch downstream retention costs. We can downsample after 7d.

alin: Open questions: 1) exact metric names agreed? 2) label set finalization? 3) owners for runtime/infra/dashboard changes?

maria: From this thread I propose names: redwood.request.errors.user.count, redwood.request.errors.internal.count, redwood.inference.fallbacks.count, redwood.runtime.oom.count, redwood.request.timeout.frontend.count, redwood.request.timeout.model.count, redwood.quota.rejections.count. Labels: env, model_family, route_group, reason, fallback_type, oom_severity, quota_type, plan_tier.

kevin: I accept those names, will start instrumenting runtime today for the reasons/labels we discussed. I'll PR the metric emitters and add tests for label cardinality.

zane: Infra will add derived rollups and draft Grafana panels. I'll post a dashboard JSON for review in #eng-platform next week.

alin: Owners: runtime=kevin, infra=zane, dashboards=maria. Action items: kevin PR by EOD Thurs, zane draft panels by next Tue, maria will write alert proposals. If anyone wants a different owner ping now.

maria: :thumbsup: I'll collect the alert rules and put them on the runbook.

kevin: FYI — I'll emit a sample payload in the PR so we can sanity-check cardinality.

alin: Thanks all. If no objections by EOD I'll lock the taxonomy and we start rollout plan.

zane: No objections from infra.

opsbot: Reminder: weekly reliability sync tomorrow 09:30 PT.

maria: Noted, will bring the alert draft.

kevin: Will link PR in the sync notes.

alin: End of thread — merging decisions into doc and runbook.
